speaker: Patient
text: 62-year-old male. The patient has recently immigrated to the US from Africa and seeks evaluation for a non-healing, red, crusty lesion on the shaft of his penis and a similar lesion on his left middle finger. Previous treatments in his home country for syphilis and eczema have been unsuccessful. The patient is a smoker, with a history of two packs per day for the last 30 years.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that information. The history of smoking, age, and the location of the penile lesion are concerning; have you noticed any bleeding, ulceration, or discharge from these areas? REQUEST TEST: Biopsy_Penile_Lesion

text: RESULTS: Biopsy_Penile_Lesion: Cells with nuclear hyperchromasia, multinucleation, and increased mitotic figures within the follicle-bearing epithelium.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Squamous Cell Carcinoma (Penis and Finger). The biopsies reveal malignant features (hyperchromasia, multinucleation, increased mitosis), and the clinical presentation of non-healing, crusted plaques on the penis and finger in a 62-year-old smoker is classic for this malignancy.
